title: How long does a red blood cell live?
hook: Millions are born every second in your bone marrow. None lasts much past four months.
summary: Without a nucleus, red blood cells carry more oxygen but cannot repair themselves, so they live about 120 days.

cardBlocks.text: Right now, your bone marrow is making roughly 2 million red blood cells every second. Production has to be that high, because each one lives only about 120 days.

To squeeze through the narrowest vessels and carry as much oxygen as possible, red blood cells give up something almost every other cell keeps: the nucleus. That frees up room for hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen, but it also leaves the cell unable to repair itself. After about four months, old red cells are removed mainly by the spleen and liver, and their iron is recycled.
With no nucleus, a red blood cell carries more oxygen but lives only about four months.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Not all blood works this way
Lacking a nucleus is a mammal trait. Birds, fish, amphibians and reptiles have red blood cells with nuclei, usually larger and oval-shaped.
The flattened disc shape, thinner in the middle, increases the surface for oxygen exchange and keeps the cell flexible enough to fold through capillaries narrower than itself.
After a blood donation, the body typically replaces the plasma volume within about a day, and the red cells over a few weeks.
